purpose: Inventory the 44 job definitions of one merge-group generation, split into executed (31) and skipped (13), with the proposition, evidence artifact, consumer, timestamps and runner-seconds of every job. The inventory is descriptive; it removes or changes nothing.

generation.whyThisGeneration: It is the observed failing merge-group generation named in the work order and it dispatches all 8 merge_group workflows, so the 44-job population is complete.

method.population: All workflow runs with event=merge_group and head_sha=5a5fbfd760d0105314e44dfdc8c64e61118c4fe5 for the 8 workflows dispatched by the merge queue.
method.enumeration: gh api "repos/Archright/Axiom/actions/runs?head_sha=<sha>&per_page=100" --paginate --slurp -> 8 workflow runs; then one jobs call per run.
method.runnerSeconds: max(0, completed_at - started_at) for executed jobs; skipped jobs contribute 0 by definition. GitHub timestamps are whole seconds.
method.countRule: 31 and 13 are measured job counts, not inferred. Per-workflow counts: admission-gate 26 (14 executed / 12 skipped); publication-integrity 10 (10/0); probe-merge-queue 2 (1/1); axiom-operational-slice 2 (2/0); bsec-integrity 1 (1/0); generation-acceptance 1 (1/0); debt-registry-gate 1 (1/0); observer-manifest-consistency 1 (1/0). Sum = 44 (31 executed / 13 skipped).
method.rawPayloads: The jobs API responses were the measurement input; the per-job timestamps and conclusions in this file are copied from them. Re-running the command above reproduces the counts.

skippedJobsSemantics.statement: Skipped jobs consume ZERO runner-seconds. A skipped job is a definition whose `if:` condition is false; GitHub marks it with conclusion=skipped at the same instant (sometimes with an inverted by-one-second timestamp), and no runner is assigned. When such a job backs a required status check, the platform reports it as success for merge purposes; it does not block the merge.
skippedJobsSemantics.consequence: Deleting skipped jobs is NOT a throughput optimization: their runner-seconds are already 0. Removing their definitions would only delete conditional paths used by other venues/stages and would not reduce the generated run time.
skippedJobsSemantics.measured: 13/13 skipped jobs have runnerSeconds=0 and runner_name null; 0 skipped jobs were assigned a runner. Executed runner-seconds (31 jobs) = 2503s.

duplicateComputationCandidates.observedOverlap: Both build verifier binaries from the same B closure; the 2026-11-03 census measured an exact B-cache hit across these jobs (docs/evidence/node24_merge_queue_critical_path_census_2026-11-03.md §5).
duplicateComputationCandidates.criterion: same proposition + same input identity + same evidence meaning, with J1-J4 all PASS
duplicateComputationCandidates.criterionStatus: NOT_MET_ON_CURRENT_EVIDENCE — same build input, but different propositions (admission witness vs operational product acceptance) and different evidence meaning; J3 cache soundness has exact-hit evidence, J1/J2/J4 are NOT_EVALUATED.
duplicateComputationCandidates.action: NONE — flagged only; no job removed or changed.

duplicateComputationCandidates.observedOverlap: Both names come from the same reusable workflow definition with different inputs.stage values; a naive reading could count them as the same computation.
duplicateComputationCandidates.criterionStatus: NOT_A_DUPLICATE_IN_EXECUTION — the stage gates are mutually exclusive (attest stage runs witness steps; verdict stage runs the predicate). The 13 verdict/* skips in this run are the stage gate, not a second execution. J1-J4 NOT_EVALUATED for any definition removal.

examinedPairs.finding: Different propositions: workflow parse-poison/shell syntax vs script-scan policy adjudication over a base..head script diff.
Same changed-file input family, but different propositions (generation acceptance vs test-scope selection) and different evidence.
observe checks src/gate/manifest.d against runner files; the App checks trust-surface blob equality. Different propositions.
Shards are a disjoint partition; license-scan is a rollup with needs on the shards, not a recomputation.

limits: Propositions and consumers are derived from the workflow definitions at the pinned callee SHAs and the repository contract; they are not a claim that every step was executed.
The `otherFailureCheckRuns` context for this generation is recorded in the WP-1 merge_group summary; this inventory does not attribute the publication-integrity/script-scan failure causes.
The inventory counts job definitions as reported by the jobs API. Reusable-workflow expansion is already reflected in the job names produced by GitHub (e.g. `attest / ...`).
Skipped-job timestamps are platform skip markers and are not execution intervals; runnerSeconds for skipped jobs is defined as 0, not computed from those timestamps.
